candidates: Proofread all text within diagram example `code` strings (node labels, comments, descriptions) for typos before merging; example code in `packages/examples/src/examples/*.ts` is shipped to end-users and visible in tools like mermaid.live.

When creating a new `package.json` that already declares `types` paths inside the `exports` field, do not also add a redundant top-level `"types"` field pointing to a different path in `dist/`. The top-level field creates conflicting type resolution and unnecessarily locks the `dist/` folder structure into the public API surface.

When adding new diagram examples to `packages/examples`, consider storing each diagram's code in a separate `.mmd` file (imported as a raw string, e.g., via Vite's `?raw` suffix) rather than as an inline TypeScript template literal. External `.mmd` files enable IDE syntax highlighting and Mermaid editor plugins for developers who maintain the examples.

In new `packages/*/tsconfig.json` files, use an explicit `"module": "Node16"` (or `"Node18"`) rather than `"module": "NodeNext"`. TypeScript 5.8+ changed the semantics of `NodeNext`, so pinning to an explicit node version avoids unexpected behaviour changes when TypeScript is upgraded.

When adding new public-facing methods to `packages/mermaid/src/mermaid.ts`, ensure the function name precisely describes what it returns or does (e.g., prefer `getRegisteredDiagramIDs` over `getRegisteredDiagramsMetadata` when only IDs are returned). If the name could be ambiguous, add a JSDoc comment that states the return type and purpose explicitly.

Each `.changeset/*.md` file should cover changes for exactly one package. If an MR touches multiple packages with distinct user-facing changes, run `pnpm changeset` once per package so that each package's `CHANGELOG.md` receives only its own relevant entry.

New packages in the monorepo that are intended to be consumed alongside an existing package (e.g., `@mermaid-js/examples` used with `mermaid`) should declare a `peerDependencies` entry with an appropriate version range so that package managers can warn users about incompatible version combinations.
